items.title: CommandLM: Data driven behavior level descriptor for ego vehicles
items.topic: CommandLM: Data driven behavior level descriptor for ego vehicles
items.summary: The arXiv paper introduces CommandLM, a multimodal large language model that generates human-readable behavior descriptions for ego vehicles from fused multi-sensor data, achieving CIDEr 0.67 and BERT-F1 0.88 on the CommandLM-nuScenes dataset. CommandLM processes temporally fused bird's-eye view representations from LiDAR and multi-camera inputs via a Q-Former adapter connected to a quantized, LoRA-fine-tuned large language model. This model is essential for safety, trust, and regulation in autonomous driving systems. The CommandLM model produces intent-aware, interpretable captions suitable for planner supervision and safety auditing.

items.title: Development of Vision-Language Model-based GNSS Spoofing Detection for Autonomous Vehicle Navigation
items.topic: Development of Vision-Language Model-based GNSS Spoofing Detection for Autonomous Vehicle Navigation
items.summary: The arXiv paper proposes CARA, a concept-aware risk attention framework for interpretable collision anticipation in autonomous driving, which derives domain-grounded risk concepts from accident narratives and aligns them with video frames via vision-language similarity. CARA organizes these concepts into evolving concept trajectories, providing explicit risk evidence that can be used for collision anticipation. The framework is intrinsically interpretable and can be used for spatio-temporal reasoning in dynamic driving scenes. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of CARA in anticipating collisions and providing interpretable reasoning.

items.title: Semantics-guided hierarchical decision-making for autonomous driving via LLM-assisted reinforcement learning
items.topic: Semantics-guided hierarchical decision-making for autonomous driving via LLM-assisted reinforcement learning
items.source: Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies
items.summary: The Transportation Research Part C: Emerging Technologies paper proposes a semantics-guided hierarchical decision-making framework for autonomous driving via LLM-assisted reinforcement learning, which enables the model to make decisions based on semantic information. The framework uses a large language model to guide the decision-making process and provide interpretable results. The authors demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework in improving the decision-making process in autonomous driving. The proposed framework can be used to improve the safety and efficiency of autonomous vehicles. The use of LLM-assisted reinforcement learning enables the model to learn from experience and adapt to new situations.
